strategy.summary: Reproduce PR #24172 (yeojohnson_llf precision loss and overflow) by building scipy at buggy commit 1b2e87dbc681, applying the developer's test_gh24172 from the PR diff, and running only that test. Success is the transition: the test fails on the buggy build and passes on the fixed build. No dependency version is documented, so the versions chosen here are inferred from the checkout's own build files and are stated as such.

system_packages: gcc or clang with C++ and Fortran compilers
BLAS/LAPACK dev headers if the checkout requires system BLAS (OpenBLAS is the usual choice)
pinned_because: No documented numpy, scipy or matplotlib constraint exists in the evidence (all era_constraints are unbounded), so no version is pinned from the evidence.

Choice of numpy: take the numpy range that the buggy checkout's pyproject.toml build-requirements and requirements/*.txt allow, and install the newest version in that range. This is an inference from repo files, not from the evidence.
matplotlib is not installed because the test does not plot; the PR reproducer's plotting is numerically irrelevant.

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/stats/tests/test_morestats.py::test_gh24172 (added by the PR diff inside the yeojohnson_llf test class, directly after test_empty). It asserts yeojohnson_llf(-14, data) and yeojohnson_llf(16, -data) both equal 12.418595783381280, and yeojohnson_llf(-20, data) equals 12.360966379200528 and yeojohnson_llf(20, -data) equals 12.380287243698629, all with rtol=1e-7, for data=[10,10,10,9.9] in float64. Apply the diff to the buggy checkout before running.
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy commit 1b2e87dbc681 with the PR test applied, test_gh24172 (numpy backend) FAILS: at least one of the four xp_assert_close calls misses the expected value beyond rtol=1e-7, or the call raises from an unsuppressed RuntimeWarning turned into an error by the scipy pytest configuration. On the fixed revision (the PR merge commit, whose hash is not in the evidence), the same command reports the test PASSED. The transition FAILED to PASSED is the whole criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: Before running the test, optionally evaluate yeojohnson_llf(-14, np.array([10,10,10,9.9])) and yeojohnson_llf(14, -data) on the buggy build to confirm the asymmetry the PR describes. This is diagnostic only and is not graded.
risks: Platform: the evidence does not show the defect is architecture-specific, but it is float64 and depends on libm log and exp behaviour. Failure on the buggy build may differ across platforms, so record the exact platform and compiler used.

Warning policy: the buggy code suppresses RuntimeWarning from np.log by substituting -inf. The fixed code does not. If the scipy pytest configuration turns warnings into errors, the failure mode on the fixed build could differ from what is expected, so check the warning filters in the checkout.

Backends: the test takes an xp fixture, so pytest may parametrise over array-api-strict and other backends. The -k filter runs all of them. Only the numpy backend is grounded by the evidence; other backends may skip or behave differently, and JAX JIT behaviour is explicitly uncertain.
Build time: a full editable scipy build is slow and needs a working Fortran toolchain. A build failure is not evidence about the bug.
Python version is not stated in the evidence (python_version null). Pick the version the buggy checkout's requires-python allows, and record it.

Unresolved in the evidence: mixed-sign data keeps the constant term and is left unchanged by the fix, so do not substitute mixed data to demonstrate the fix. Discussion also notes possible further issues when sigma^2 is very small and data is clustered at zero, which are unresolved and not covered by this test.
Fixed-commit identity is not in the evidence. Confirm the PR merge commit from the PR page before claiming the pass transition.

oracle.reference_source: Expected values in test_gh24172 were computed with mpmath at mp.dps=100 (per the test comment)
oracle.why: The developer test compares against mpmath-derived constants with a relative tolerance, so the pass/fail decision is made by that tolerance on the four asserted values.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The buggy _yeojohnson_llf computes the constant term and takes np.log of the variance directly, and substitutes -inf when variance is too low. At lmb=-14/16 this loses precision, and at lmb=-20/20 the log-variance term overflows. Either path can push a value outside rtol=1e-7 of the expected constant, or raise through an unsuppressed warning, so the test fails. The exact failing assertion is not stated in the evidence.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: The fixed code drops the constant term for all-positive or all-negative data, computes the log-variance in the log domain (modelled on boxcox_llf), and uses xp.finfo(dtype).eps for the abs(lmb) threshold. The four asserted values then agree with the mpmath references within rtol=1e-7, so the test passes.
